Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: 4 stars — four years of use, but read this before buying 3.2

Four stars. Murmur has been essential to making Lanternfolk, but I can’t give it five with the current save-loading bug and no further support from its creator. If you’re considering buying it now, please read the warning below before spending your money.

I bought Murmur in August 2022 for $19. The first Lanternfolk prototype was literally just the ferryman scene, made in one weekend with this plugin. That was the weekend the game started feeling like something I could actually make, rather than something I talked about making. It was also when I quit my job at a mobile studio. Murmur didn’t make that decision for me, obviously, but being able to build that scene mattered a lot. Honestly, I don’t think Lanternfolk would exist without it.

Four years later, we have 412 dialogue nodes and nine languages using Murmur’s CSV export. It’s been part of the actual work of making this game, not just a tool I liked during a jam and then forgot about. That’s what my rating reflects. It is not a clean bill of health for the version currently on sale.

The important warning: 3.2.0 resets Murmur variables to their defaults when loading saves made in 3.1.x, in our testing. In Lanternfolk, that means the ferryman forgets you already paid him, among other things. This is a serious compatibility bug, not a cosmetic annoyance. I reported it in the forum on 19 October. I suspected a change in how save keys are identified, but that was a guess, not a confirmed diagnosis.

Rolling back to 3.1.4 fixed it for us, and another user confirmed the same result. The rollback is to replace the Murmur folder inside your project’s addons folder with the folder from the 3.1.4 release. Back up your project and saves first. Keep a copy of 3.1.4 and don’t update it to 3.2. Our old saves load correctly again on 3.1.4. I can’t promise this repairs every save problem, or that saves created in 3.2 will work after rolling back.

For new buyers: the listing is currently $29, 3.2 is the latest release, and Ines has said she is stepping back and won’t be fixing this bug. Don’t buy expecting an official patch or ongoing support. If you need a maintained plugin and someone available to help when things break, that is a very good reason to choose something else.

I understand the bad reviews about broken saves. People have lost time, and they deserve to know what they’re buying. But I think grimbyte’s “took our money and ran” review is cruel. I paid $19 and got four years of updates and a tool that helped me build my game. That doesn’t cancel out the broken release. It also doesn’t make “the dev clearly doesn’t care” a fair conclusion.

The source is now available under MIT, so someone can fork it. Maybe I’ll have a look myself after launch, but that’s a possibility, not a maintenance promise or something buyers should count on.

Thank you, Ines, for Murmur. It helped me make something I care about. I’m disappointed by where the last release leaves things, and grateful for the years before it. Both are true.
